decisions.name: Width576 integer-serving expansion
decisions.reason: The retained wide artifact has weak actual replies and the fixed complete-prefix pair is running. Its endpoint supplies the next useful-artifact decision; widening formats now would not supply low-bit fidelity or D5 efficiency. This is a research prioritization finding, not a new programme gate or automatic requirement for broad qualification.

decisions.name: Shared signed4 runtime representation for supported128/256
decisions.reason: Existing source expands packed four-bit weights into i16 vectors, retains them in a map, then deep-clones the eleven signed4 weight arrays into cached fields. Sharing packed storage and directly indexing the already-compatible product tables can remove this demonstrated duplication without changing learned arrays, model equations, shape support or artifacts.

serving_contract.owner_scope: Native learned geometric model with multiplier-free served numerical kernel; no adoption here of converted transformer serving or hardware-multiplier exceptions. Offline floating Rust learning remains permitted.
serving_contract.D0_b: At most four-bit multiplicative learned weights with dyadic scales; integer/add/subtract/shift/table execution and no floating/transcendental serving computation or multiplier instructions in the declared kernel. Existing signed16 additive offsets stay additive; do not reinterpret scalar policy.
serving_contract.D5: Terminal per-token learned-parameter sparsity remains live. Dense coefficient traversal remains noncompliant with that end state even when the same coefficients occupy fewer bytes.
serving_contract.output_projection: The width576 tied output map visits4096*576=2359296 learned embedding coefficients/token, over43percent of5429826 total parameters, before recurrent/update maps. Recurrence-only factorization is not a solution to this dense output access.

width576_barriers.barrier: Separate strict576/read64/context256 Quaternion/Dot recovery is continuous Full only; its checkpoint loader rejects quantization. It does not relax canonical/integer loading.
Embedding/vocabulary indexing and row blocks explicitly support128/256 strides.
Current affine input lengths are128/256/512. Width576 and concatenated update width1152 need substantive arithmetic/kernel work.
RMS variance encodes division by128/256 with fixed shifts. Width576 needs specified fixed-point division, rounding and bounds; changing a shape enum is insufficient.
Partitioned conversation is explicitly256/Dot, with fixed VAL_DIM256,768-element affine buffers and512-coordinate product scratch.
Packed export is F32 emulation, not serving. Generic code generation or a successfully written file does not prove reload: the packed loader applies canonical shape validation.

separate_session_paths.ordinary: IntegerSession plus IntegerModel::step is the ordinary bounded-context numerical path. The fourth-lab exact-ID TextSession/DialogueConversation adapter preserves generated IDs, pending tokens and sampler continuity over that path.
separate_session_paths.google_partitioned: SessionState plus step_conversational_into/ChatSession is the separate partitioned persistent/rolling/L2 conversation path with additional zeta/Hopf-related state. It is guarded to width256/Dot. Representation optimization must preserve its existing behavior; ordinary-session equivalence is not proof of its memory/reasoning claims.
separate_session_paths.review_implication: Both paths consume the same Parameter storage in different branches, so all consumers must migrate consistently. Do not silently redirect one session type to the other or expand shape/capability claims.

packed_opportunity.current_representation: Signed4 artifact bytes are expanded to Vec<i16>. Parameter derives Clone, and get_param clones11 signed4 weight parameters into p_* caches while map originals remain.
packed_opportunity.proposed_representation: Private immutable shared packed signed4 backing storage, referenced by map and cached fields. Hot matrix/vocabulary paths use low/high nibble directly as product-table indices. Keep signed16 additive data unchanged.
packed_opportunity.storage_arithmetic: For duplicated signed4 code payload only: two copies*2bytes/code -> one shared0.5byte/code, eightfold smaller. One active coefficient stream2bytes/code ->0.5byte/code, fourfold fewer coefficient bytes.
packed_opportunity.limitations: These are representation-byte calculations, not measured whole-model RSS, cache traffic, latency, energy, sparsity or quality gains. Product tables, state, metadata and dense coefficient visits remain.

concrete_risks.requirement: Arc/shared handles must refer to the same backing data across parameter map and cached fields. No retained full signed4 i16 mirror and no per-hot-call whole-row unpacking. Tied embedding/output projection continues to use identical codes.
Direct table index0..7/9..15 is correct for0..7/-7..-1. Scalar embedding input and output.norm.weight need signed decoding in place. Do not feed unsigned9..15 as positive scalar coefficients.
Reject nibble8 (-8), invalid lengths and nonzero unused high nibble before validated storage exists. Product-table slot8 is zero, so bypassing import validation could silently change arithmetic.
Preserve low-nibble-first coordinate order,128/256 row widths and512 concatenated affine width, including unrolled8-row/4-row blocks and tail rows. No row boundary interleaving.

Keep row exponents, i64 dot bounds, Q40 scaling, bias addition, rounding and saturation locations unchanged. Existing supported bounds make integer dot terms exact; no approximate accumulation is introduced.

No new on-disk schema, byte rewrite, hash/identity change, quantizer change or width576 admission. Preserve existing public decoded-loader callers when introducing the private runtime representation; share validation rather than weaken it.

Avoid per-coordinate abstraction dispatch, bounds-check overhead and row expansion that negate smaller storage. Preserve blocked product-table reuse. Smaller storage is established by representation; speed/energy await measured execution.

Runtime specialist owns the narrow integer representation/model integration in isolated radial-transfer-validation checkout. Principal coordinates shared source ownership and schedules builds/model work. Frozen dialogue source, campaigns, artifacts and running processes remain unchanged.

packed-integer-arithmetic-review.json.reviewer: Fourth-lab geometry and arithmetic research specialist
packed-integer-arithmetic-review.json.scope: Completed read-only review of signed4 coefficient storage, packed dot kernels and their focused test expectations. Broader model integration is independently owned. This receipt records that review without new checks or experiments.

source_binding.reviewed_state: Completed first implementation as uncommitted working-tree changes against this base; hashes identify the exact reviewed file contents, not an assertion about later edits.

findings.reasoning: from_decoded accepts [-7,7], stores the earlier coefficient in the low nibble and sign-extends the selected nibble through i8 shifts. The unused high nibble for an odd element count is zero. Signed16 rejects its reserved minimum.

The unchanged artifact decoder rejects nibble8 (-8) and nonzero unused high padding before repacking. Repacking independently rejects decoded values outside [-7,7]. The table entry at index8 is therefore unreachable for an admitted coefficient.

findings.source: packed_rows.rs:109-125; model.rs matrix_work_direct_into, affine_direct_into and vocabulary dispatch
findings.reasoning: packed_range checks start+length overflow, even coefficient alignment and logical element bounds before producing byte slices. Traced production callers supply exact supported128/256/512 input widths, with product length guards. All are divisible by8, so the generic kernel has no unprocessed remainder. Its raw internal slice API assumes these validated lengths rather than constituting a general checked dot-product boundary.

The generic kernel retains eight coordinate-class accumulators and the same final grouping. Eight width256 rows use128 packed bytes each and retain consecutive two-coordinate sums. Four width512 rows use256 bytes each, preserve the original four-coordinate grouping and two accumulators per row. Nibble extraction changes representation, not coefficient order.

For validated coefficients with absolute value<=7 and product tables constructed from i32 inputs, every512-term dot has absolute-sum bound512*7*2^31=7696581394432<2^43, far inside i64. Intermediate subsets/pair sums are bounded by the same absolute sum. No rounding is introduced during nibble extraction/table accumulation; existing dyadic scaling and quantization remain downstream. This bound does not certify arbitrary caller-supplied i64 table contents.

focused_tests_source_review.independent_reference: Kernel expected values multiply original decoded i16 coefficients by original i32 inputs in i64 and sum them; expected packed bytes are also literal constants. These references do not derive their expected dots through the new packed decoder.
covered_cases: Literal byte order for every valid signed4 code and odd final padding
Reserved codes, unsupported bit width, odd/aligned/outside/overflow ranges and signed16 endpoints
Full i32 extremes and mixed signs/zero
128/256/512 matrix dispatch, nine-row blocked groups plus tails, per-row scales and bias
128/256 embedding rows at vocabulary endpoints and all vocabulary projection rows
Packed embedding product tables versus independently checked decoded values
Arc allocation sharing for cloned coefficient storage
focused_tests_source_review.scope_limit: Tests reuse existing scaling/quantization functions for those unchanged downstream operations; they are independent references for the changed packing and accumulation boundary, not a fresh independent numerical specification for the whole model.

conclusion.readiness: No blocking source defect found in the reviewed representation and kernels. Ready for the principal-declared functional and actual-output checks; this is not an executed parity or performance result.
conclusion.claim_boundary: Packing preserves intended dense access semantics and reduces coefficient representation size. It does not implement conditional parameter routing or establish D5 compliance, throughput or energy gains.
